patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Teams and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Microsoft Teams only if your buying job matches “M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on ” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than Microsoft Teams's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Teams leans shared coverage; Vonage leans business-phone, sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Teams and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Microsoft Teams is M365 collaboration hub (chat, meetings, files) with optional Teams Phone telephony add-on — free Teams tier exists; Phone Standard ~$10/user; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Teams (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Teams-leaning — vs Vonage-leaning business-phone, sales-calling.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Teams — Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — Microsoft Teams: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job; Teams Phone requires an eligible Teams/M365 licence plus PSTN (PAYG or Calling Plan); Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Teams is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Scored as a collaboration hub — Teams Phone is a telephony add-on, not the primary scored job · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid Microsoft Teams if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
